Description: Frontend experience for clients and bank managers: application submission, tracking, review, decision support, and form presentation.
As a bank manager, I want to see every submitted application and review its details so that I can approve or deny the loan.

Title 3: Build the manager review queue with portfolio stats, search, status filters and sorting
Description: Deliver the manager's entry point: a protected console that lists every submitted application together with portfolio KPIs, and lets the manager narrow the queue by status, keyword and sort order. It turns the stored applications into a workable review list and is where status changes become visible. Acceptance: a signed-in manager sees the live queue with correct KPI counts, can combine a status filter with a text search and a sort, and can open any row.

Title 3: Implement the review drawer with eligibility scoring, proof-of-income preview and the approve/deny decision
Description: Deliver the complete file-review experience: a side drawer that consolidates the applicant's identity, financial situation, requested terms, computed eligibility score and uploaded proof of income in one place. From there the manager can inspect the document and record an auditable approve or deny decision without leaving the queue. Acceptance: the manager can read the full file, open the uploaded document, record a decision, and see the updated status and audit fields immediately.
As a client, I want to submit my loan application so that the bank can review my request.

Title 3: Implement the submit flow: step validation, reference generation and persistence
Description: Deliver the end-to-end submission path: validate every step, assemble the application payload, create the request through the API with a unique reference and persist it so it immediately reaches the manager's review queue. The task guarantees that only complete, valid applications can be submitted and that a submission is never duplicated. Acceptance: a valid form produces exactly one persisted application with a unique reference, and an invalid form is blocked with field-level messages.

Title 3: Build the confirmation screen and the client tracking timeline
Description: Deliver the post-submission experience: an immediate confirmation showing the generated reference and estimated payment, followed by a tracking area where the client can follow every request through its status, timeline and final manager decision. Acceptance: after submitting, the client sees a confirmation with the reference, and the same request appears in "My requests" with the correct live status and decision details.
As a client, I want to enter my personal, financial and loan details so that the bank can assess my request.

Title 3: Implement the applicant step with CNIB, age, occupation, family and employment inputs
Description: Deliver the identity step of the form: capture and validate the applicant's personal, family and professional details, including the 18-digit CNIB and age limits, before any financial information is requested. This establishes who is applying and whether they meet the basic intake conditions. Acceptance: the applicant cannot leave step 1 with a missing name/occupation, an invalid CNIB or an out-of-range age, and valid values are carried into the submission payload.

Title 3: Implement the finances and loan-term steps with live payment and debt-ratio assessment
Description: Deliver the financial and loan-term steps: capture income, existing debt, savings, payment history and the requested amount, duration and purpose, then turn them into a live affordability assessment. The client sees the estimated installment, debt ratio and eligibility signals update as they type, so the request is informed before submission. Acceptance: changing amount, duration, income or debt immediately updates the estimate, and the assessment reflects the documented rules (age, verified income, DTI ≤ 40%, missed payments ≤ 2, plus advisory checks).
As a client, I want a clear, usable application form so that I can complete my request without confusion.

Title 3: Build the responsive three-step form layout, stepper and sticky summary panel
Description: Deliver the form's presentation shell: a responsive three-step experience with a clear progress stepper, consistent visual hierarchy and a summary panel that stays alongside the fields on desktop and stacks on mobile. It makes the application readable and navigable at any screen size. Acceptance: the form is usable at desktop and mobile widths, the active step is obvious, and the summary stays visible without overlapping the fields.

Title 3: Implement reusable field controls and the drag-and-drop proof-of-income upload
Description: Deliver the form's input building blocks: a consistent set of labelled fields with validation states, plus a mandatory proof-of-income upload that supports drag-and-drop, type and size checks, image compression and an inline preview. These components keep every step visually and behaviourally consistent. Acceptance: a client can attach a valid PDF/JPG/PNG by browsing or dropping it, sees a clear preview, gets an explicit error for an invalid type/size, and cannot submit without the document.
